subject: MetricWorks performance validation and load/latency checklist
messages:
From: Alejandra Soto <alejandra.soto@metricworks.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Performance validation and load testing for Redwood

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move toward procurement, our infrastructure team needs a short but specific validation plan that demonstrates Redwood's latency and throughput characteristics under our expected workload. High-level asks: 

- 99th and 95th percentile token latency samples for single-turn generation at 16k and 8k max-seq lengths.
- Sustained throughput (tokens/sec and requests/sec) at several concurrency targets (50 qps, 200 qps, 500 qps).
- Cold-start behavior and replica warmup time.
- Impact of prefix/KV cache on tail latency for chat-style sessions.
- Test methodology details: hardware, model variants, batching, and any synthetic traffic tooling you use.

We'd like to run a short pilot next week (2–3 days). Can you share a short checklist or plan we can include in the RFP response? Procurement will need any supporting SLO matrix and a sample CSV of latency traces.

Best,
Alejandra
Alejandra Soto
Head of Infrastructure, MetricWorks

Hi Alejandra — thanks, and glad the demo was useful.

I've attached a compact benchmarking checklist and proposed pilot schedule (metricworks_bench_plan_v1.pdf). The plan gives:

- A minimal test matrix (models, concurrency, sequence lengths).
- Exact instrumentation points (client timestamps, server-side token timestamps, and tracing hooks).
- Warmup and cold-start definitions we use so results are comparable.
- Deliverables: SLO table (xlsx), sample latency trace (csv), and a short runbook for the pilot.

We can run the pilot in your cloud account (private deployment) or in our hosted env. If you prefer private, we'll need minimal network access and a short allowlist window. Proposed pilot dates: July 6–8 — does that work for you?

I'll loop in our infra/bench experts to confirm the test matrix.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>

Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Performance validation and load testing for Redwood

Karthik / Neha — forwarding MetricWorks note. Key asks: 99/95 pctl token latencies at 8k/16k, sustained throughput at 50/200/500 qps, cold-start behavior, and KV cache impact for chat sessions. They want short artifacts for procurement (SLO table + sample CSV).

Can you confirm the following and attach the minimal artifacts?
- Test matrix: models (gpt-compat low-latency + 7B quantized), batch sizes, target concurrency points.
- Hardware we will run in pilot (GPU SKU variants) and any expected perf delta.
- Warmup criteria: how many minutes/requests to consider warmed?
- Approach for prefix cache evaluation (simulate user sessions with N-turns).
- Deliverable filenames: redwood_latency_snapshot.csv and slo-matrix.xlsx

Aim for a concise one-page plan to share with Alejandra.

Marissa
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: Performance validation and load testing for Redwood

Marissa / Neha —

Quick draft of the matrix (attaching artifacts): slo-matrix.xlsx (SLO targets and acceptance), redwood_latency_snapshot.csv (example traces). Summary:

- Models: rw-llm-7b-qat (quantized low-latency), rw-llm-13b-pt (fp16), and a smaller 3B baseline for comparison.
- Hardware: A100 80GB (baseline), A10G (cost-focused), and dedicated T4 for small model runs. Expect ~1.8x higher 99p on A10G vs A100 for 13B; 3B is ~2.5x faster.
- Concurrency targets: 50, 200, 500 QPS. Batch policy: adaptive batching with max batch size per GPU set to preserve tail.
- Sequence lengths: 512, 4096, 8192 tokens; measure tokens/sec and request/sec.
- Warmup: define warm after 120s of steady-state or 5000 tokens generated, whichever first. Cold-start measurement: first-request latency after a 10-minute idle.
- KV/prefix cache test: generate sessions of 1, 3, and 10 turns with 90/10 token overlap to measure cache hit impact on 99p.

I'll attach the two files to the plan. If Marissa wants, I can also produce a short script that replays their sample distribution.

Karthik
Senior Performance Engineer

Hi Alejandra —

Thanks for the ask. Attached is a short, customer-friendly version of the pilot plan and the artifacts Karthik prepared (metricworks_bench_plan_v1.pdf, redwood_latency_snapshot.csv, slo-matrix.xlsx). Highlights:

- Pilot scope: 3 days, run in your environment (recommended) or hosted. We will execute three concurrent matrices (3B/7B/13B) across A100/A10G.
- Deliverables: 99/95/50 pctl token latency table by seq-length, tokens/sec at targeted qps, cold-start samples, and a short summary of KV cache benefit.
- Acceptance: 99p latency and tokens/sec are compared to agreed targets in slo-matrix.xlsx.
- Next steps: please share a representative traffic CSV (one-line-per-request with seq-length and token estimates) and confirm whether you prefer July 6–8 or July 8–10.

On Wed, Jul 1, 2026, 09:12 AM, Karthik Iyer wrote:
> Summary of matrix: rw-llm-7b-qat, rw-llm-13b-pt, A100/A10G/T4, warmup=120s or 5k tokens, KV test=1/3/10-turn sessions.

If you can share the traffic sample and a short allowlist window for private deployment, we'll book infra and produce the artifacts for procurement.

Thanks,
Marissa
